findings.description: The KMS key protecting audit trail data omits enable_key_rotation, which defaults to false, so the key material is never automatically rotated. Long-lived static key material increases the blast radius of a key compromise and fails common compliance requirements for audit log encryption keys.

No policy argument is defined, so AWS applies the default KMS key policy granting kms:* to the account root principal. Any IAM principal in the account that can be granted IAM permissions may then use or administer the audit-trail encryption key, including decrypting audit data or scheduling key deletion, with no least-privilege separation between key administrators and key users.

deletion_window_in_days is set to the minimum of 7 days, leaving only a brief window to detect and cancel an unauthorised or accidental key deletion. If this key is destroyed, all audit trail data encrypted under it becomes permanently unrecoverable, which is an attractive anti-forensics target for an attacker with kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion (which the default root key policy effectively permits).
